newsitem.title: FRANCE: European group accuses Portugal of police violence.
newsitem.headline: European group accuses Portugal of police violence.

text.p: The European Committee against Torture accused Portuguese police on Thursday of frequently mistreating people in their custody, saying the most common abuse was blows inflicted with fists or clubs.

The committee, an experts' body charged with ensuring respect for the European Convention to Prevent Torture and Inhuman or Degrading Treatments, levelled the accusations in a report following a visit to Portugal from May 14-26, 1995.
The report contained a reply from the Portuguese government saying it was worried about the phenomenon of police brutality but that it was less widespread than alleged in the report.
"A significant number of the people we questioned said they were mistreated when held by police," the report said.
The body was allowed to visit police lockups and jails and said it noted the presence there of "many staves or clubs that were different from those issued to police as normal equipment".
The committee said it had seen little improvement in the situation since 1992, when it paid a first visit to Portugal and concluded that police mistreated suspects relatively frequently.
It said there was overcrowding in prisons in Lisbon, Linho and Oporto, although efforts had been made in the first two prisons to improve conditions of detention.
The committee singled out Portugal's public security police and the judicial police's Lisbon prison for particular criticism, with the Republican Guard coming in for milder criticism.
The Portuguese government response said that problems were most widespread in rundown areas, where delinquency and drug trafficking and use were acute problems.
It said police worked in particularly difficult conditions in Lisbon and Oporto.
